title: Family wants answers after man shot and killed by RCMP on Montreal Lake Cree Nation
subtitle: His sister identified the man as 28-year-old Dillon McDonald.
article: The family of a 28-year-old man who died after he was shot on Tuesday night by RCMP on Montreal Lake Cree Nation wants answers, his sister says.
Chantel McDonald identified the man as her brother, Dillon McDonald. They lost their eldest brother two weeks ago, and "now he's gone" too, she said.
"(W)hat had happened to him was tragic & traumatizing to watch," she wrote in a Facebook message to the StarPhoenix on Wednesday evening.
On Wednesday, tributes to her brother poured in on social media, with people offering condolences to her family.

The shooting is now under investigation by Saskatoon city police, who sent investigators out to Montreal Lake on Wednesday morning.
An RCMP media release did not identify Dillon McDonald as the man who was shot about five hours after officers went to a home on Montreal Lake Cree Nation.

The release said officers responded to a call shortly before 5 p.m. and had been told an armed man had "barricaded himself" in the home after allegedly "using the firearm to chase another individual out."
The man was holding a firearm when he left the house around 10:15 p.m., the release alleged.
"Responding police officers discharged their firearms and injured the man."

RCMP attempted life-saving measures until local emergency medical services arrived, the release stated. The man was taken to Victoria Hospital in Prince Albert, where he was declared dead around 11 p.m.
The RCMP requested an independent investigation observer be appointed by Saskatchewan's Ministry of Justice.

Earlier this year, legislation to create an independent investigative arm of the Public Complaints Commission was passed. The Serious Incident Response Team, which is not yet operational, is to conduct investigations into serious incidents, including ones involving sexual assault, serious injury or deaths in police custody or as a result of a police officer's actions.
SIRT's creation would end the practice of police investigating police in serious incidents. Saskatchewan is one of the last provinces in Canada to create such a body.
Initially, the team was expected to be up and running this fall.

In a November email to the StarPhoenix, the ministry of justice said SIRT's executive director and administrative staff were "concentrating on laying the groundwork for establishing SIRT" and once that work is complete, it will be operational.
This work is supposed to be finished by the end of the fiscal year.

The Ministry of Justice has appointed two investigation observers and both the executive director of SIRT and the Ministry of Corrections, Policing and Public Safety have been notified of the incident in Montreal Lake.
"In the future, we expect the Serious Incident Response Team (SIRT) will provide independent oversight in situations such as this one," the ministry said.
